messages:
miyu: quick heads-up — aurora-slim-v2 P4A quant bring-up shows strange grapheme-clumping in mixed JP/KR long-context evals (>1024). samples attached, looks like joiner behavior around ruby/kelvin-style annotations.

rahul: numbers? how big is the regression? :thinking:

miyu: short summary: baseline fp16 -> BLEU 29.1, chrF 0.684; P4A quant -> BLEU 26.2 (-2.9), chrF 0.634 (-0.05), JER +7.1% on ja test. overall 3% drop in sacrebleu on longctx subset. eval-bot: run-id aurora-slimv2-p4a-20260320-1422 finished.

ciara: can you paste a compact sample diff?

miyu: sure — example below (source contains kanji + ruby + hangul interleaving):

```
REF: 新宿(しんじゅく)駅에서 버スに 탑승했습니다。
FP16: 新宿(しんじゅく)駅에서 バスに 탑승しました。
P4A: 新宿(しんじゅく)駅에서버スに탑승しました。
```
\nnotice missing spaces and kana compressed into kanji token boundaries — looks like tokenizer merges shifted.

shawn: interesting. does this appear only after kv-cache warmup? or right from token 0?

miyu: mostly after ~300 tokens (longctx). shortctx (<256) looks fine. hypothesis: cache-aligned batching + per-token scale in P4A leads to a boundary rounding error when we reconstruct subtoken offsets.

rahul: can you share the token ids for that sample (both encodings)? want to see whether encode() differs between fp16 and P4A path or if it's a decode-only issue.

ciara: grabbed tokenizer output from the run:

```
# tokenizer.encode(source)
FP16 ids: [1023, 4567, 890, 77, 12, 334, 9001]
P4A ids: [1023, 4567, 890, 77, 12, 334, 9001]
# tokenizer offsets (fp16): [(0,2),(2,6),(6,8),(8,9),(9,11),(11,14),(14,18)]
# tokenizer offsets (p4a): [(0,2),(2,6),(6,8),(8,9),(9,14),(14,18)]
```
\nciara: offsets differ — p4a shows a merged offset (9,14) collapsing two subtokens into one offset, which explains merged output.

shawn: that points to a decode step bug rather than encode. maybe the kv-assembly that maps kv cache indices to byte offsets is dropping a boundary when quant scales are applied. can someone repro with kv-cache disabled?

miyu: repro command I used:

```
# run a short reproducer on staging
./run_eval.sh --model aurora-slim-v2 --quant p4a --max-tokens 2048 --kv-cache true --batch 16 --seed 42
```
\nmiyu: logs include this repeated warning from serving runtime:

```
WARN kvcache: eviction_align_mismatch at step=18 shard=3 delta=2
```
\nmiyu: when I flip --kv-cache false the warning goes away and outputs match fp16 on that sample (BLEU gap narrows to ~0.4).

rahul: good triage. so two axes: P4A per-token scaling interacting with kv-cache assembly. try forcing single-batch and single-worker to rule out cross-shard reorder: `--batch 1 --workers 1` and `--disable-prefetch` please. also rerun with small synthetic where we manually craft offsets to force a boundary.

ciara: added to run-queue. also noting this only hits mixed-script cases where grapheme clusters straddle subtoken boundaries (ruby + hangul join). might be low-frequency but high-cost for QA teams.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: aurora-slim-v2-p4a-canary -> staging (2 replicas) by miyu at 2026-03-20T14:40Z.

shawn: if repro is consistent, plan: 1) patch kvcache assembly to use 64-bit offset accumulator (avoids rounding when scale applied), 2) add unit that fuzzes grapheme cluster boundaries under quant. 3) add regression test to eval harness covering mixed JP-KR ruby sequences.

miyu: agreed. I'll open a lightweight PR with logs and the reproducer + sample set. putting triage label and blocking any rollout to dedicated until we have a fix.

rahul: thanks — please add a quick note to the release checklist to run the mixedscript smoke suite for any future quant compiler changes. :+1:

ciara: FYI adding a small eval metric to console: highlight per-locale chrF delta and a per-sample boundary-failure count so SRE can set an alert if it spikes.

miyu: thanks all, will post PR link and a minimal failing test when ready.
